name: Lilongwe
subtitle: Lilongwe, capital of Malawi: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: About 989,318 people live in Lilongwe city (counted 2018).
Lilongwe is named after the river that runs through the city and has been an administrative centre since 1904.
Its importance as an agricultural market centre grew in the 1920s, linked to a tobacco industry in its hinterland and its position at a road junction.

parts.text: Lilongwe is named after the river that runs through the city and has been an administrative centre since 1904.
Its importance as an agricultural market centre grew in the 1920s, linked to a tobacco industry in its hinterland and its position at a road junction.
Malawi became independent in 1964 with Hastings Banda as first prime minister.
The government decided in 1965 to move the capital from Zomba to Lilongwe, one year after independence, but the move was not completed until 1975.
Construction of Capital Hill, the site of central government, began in 1969; the first master plan (1968) was prepared with South African planners and envisaged a garden city.
The zoning scheme divides the city into four sectors: Old Town, Capital Hill, Kanengo and Lumbadzi.

parts.text: 989,318 in 2018, according to the figures compiled from the national statistics office. Which area is counted matters: Persons enumerated in Lilongwe City in the 2018 Population and Housing Census (conducted September 2018); area given as 403.3 km2 in the NSO density table; 17,563,749 enumerated nationally.

items.text: Lilongwe becomes an administrative centre under colonial rule.
Lilongwe grows as an agricultural market centre as tobacco farming emerges around it.
Government decides to relocate the capital from Zomba to Lilongwe.
Construction of Capital Hill begins, after the first master plan of 1968.
Lilongwe supersedes Zomba as capital, followed by high population growth in the 1970s and 1980s.
The Parliament Building on Capital Hill is opened, funded by a Chinese grant.
Census enumerates 989,318 people in Lilongwe City.
